records.title: Email to Loosemores (successor to John Loosemore & Co.) (26 May 2026)
records.description: Public-safe extract of a sent email to Loosemores on 26 May 2026 requesting preservation of surviving archival material concerning Great House Farm and BP Properties Ltd v Buckler.

provenance.holder: Cedwyn email archive (read-only export of the family mailbox)

records.transcript_status: public-safe extract; exact preservation request reproduced; personal narrative, video link and personal identifiers omitted
records.transcript:
Sirs / Madam,

I am a family descendant connected to Great House Farm, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan, and an heir of the family historically associated with the property.
I am researching historical litigation and events surrounding:

BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

Earlier proceedings involving Great House Farm

Proceedings involving Mrs Mary Williams / Mrs Frederick Buckler

Licence correspondence circa 1974

Great House Farm, Llandough near Penarth

BP Properties Ltd / BP Pension Trust / related entities where relevant.

I would be grateful if your firm could check whether any archived material survives, including but not limited to:

Case files
Attendance notes
Instructions / briefs
Witness statements
Counsel papers
Title investigations
Deeds packets
Land correspondence
Licence letters
Photographs
Maps / plans
Press files
Internal memoranda
Storage references
Archive indexes
Destruction schedules / destruction logs

I understand retention periods may have expired. If files no longer exist, I would be grateful for confirmation of whether records once existed, approximate destruction date, retention policy applied, and any successor archive location or off-site storage reference.

Please treat this correspondence as a request to preserve any surviving archival material pending further enquiries.

[Personal family narrative, allegations, video link and personal identifiers omitted from this public-safe extract.]

Forest of Cardiff,

I am writing concerning the woodland area at Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near St Dochdwy's Church and the later Church View Close development.

[Other ownership-history and personal context from the original message is omitted from this public-safe extract.]

Please therefore confirm:

   12. Please preserve any historical records you hold concerning this land, including correspondence, agreements, plans, invoices, photographs and instructions from landowners or developers.

For clarity, this correspondence is intended to put Forest of Cardiff on notice that ownership of the land is disputed.

I would be grateful for a substantive response and for confirmation that relevant historical records will be retained pending resolution of the ownership issue.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

records.transcript:
Dear Sirs,

I write as Sion Buckler. The public working evidence catalogue is at https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com, with the title and chronology index at https://dartboard.bucklerfamily.estate and the long-term archive at https://wayback.bucklerfamily.estate.

BP Properties Ltd v Buckler concerned Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth. Possession was obtained on 29 November 1988; the outbuildings were demolished on 30 November 1988 and the farmhouse on 5–6 December 1988. Before considering any litigation, I am exhausting all non-litigious avenues and placing preservation notices with every party that may hold records or artefacts.

If your firm acted for BP Properties Ltd, the BP Pension Trust or any related entity in that matter, please preserve and do not destroy any client files, correspondence, court bundles, title documents, photographs, plans or other material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr for 1969 to present. Please confirm in writing whether you hold any such material and that a preservation hold is in place.

Kind regards,

Sion Buckler
(Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
[email address redacted]
